title: Finite inertia gives an adequate coarse moduli space
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\mathcal X$ a finite-type algebraic stack over $k$ in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Suppose its inertia $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ is finite, where $I_{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ parametrizes an object together with an automorphism. There exist an algebraic space $Q/k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and a surjective morphism $q:\mathcal X\to Q$ which is an adequate moduli space and a coarse moduli space. The latter means that composition with $q$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_k(Q,T)\simeq\operatorname{Mor}_k(\mathcal X,T)$ for every algebraic space $T/k$, and that $\pi_0(\mathcal X(\Omega))\to Q(\Omega)$ is bijective for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. If the diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ is finite, then $Q$ is separated over $k$, meaning that its diagonal is a closed immersion. Finite for representable morphisms and finite type are tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No smoothness or invertibility-of-order assumption is made on the inertia.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), Tag 0DUY (lemma-keel-mori-diagonal), in the relative k-setting; Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 Section 8, Theorem 8.1.1 and Proposition 8.2.1 (coarse morphism is adequate), printed pp.37--38, read online; local Alper PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-inertia-etale-affine-charts] to $\mathcal X$. Its hypothesis is exactly the given finiteness of the inertia morphism, not just finiteness of stabilizers at geometric points. Obtain a small jointly surjective family $g_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$ of representable separated etale stabilizer-preserving maps and presentations $\mathcal X_i=[U_i/R_i]$ with $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}E_i$, $R_i=\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, and finite locally free projections. Every object in this construction is over $k$.

For each $i$ put $C_i=\operatorname{Eq}(E_i\rightrightarrows L_i)$ and $M_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$. The finite-flat affine-groupoid theorem supplies $f_i:\mathcal X_i\to M_i$, uniform categorical, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and a universal homeomorphism, with bijections on geometric isomorphism classes. It also supplies $\mathcal O_{M_i}\simeq(f_i)_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_i}$; its flat equalizer formula will remain valid on etale affine charts. Thus neither the structure sheaf assertion nor arbitrary algebraic-space universality is being inferred from the definition of invariants alone.

Set $\mathcal X_{ij}=\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_j$. By the permanence clause of [lem-sfb-etale-stabilizer-preserving-affine-moduli], both projections are representable separated etale and stabilizer-preserving. Apply that lemma to the projection to $\mathcal X_i$, obtaining $f_{ij}:\mathcal X_{ij}\to M_{ij}$ and a cartesian square over a separated etale map $M_{ij}\to M_i$. Applying it to the other projection gives $\widetilde f_{ij}:\mathcal X_{ij}\to\widetilde M_{ij}$ and the corresponding square over $M_j$. Categoricality supplies unique maps $a:M_{ij}\to\widetilde M_{ij}$ and $b:\widetilde M_{ij}\to M_{ij}$ with $af_{ij}=\widetilde f_{ij}$ and $b\widetilde f_{ij}=f_{ij}$. Thus $(ba)f_{ij}=f_{ij}$ and $(ab)\widetilde f_{ij}=\widetilde f_{ij}$, so uniqueness gives $ba=1$ and $ab=1$. Transport the second square along this isomorphism; its bottom map is $M_{ij}\xrightarrow{a}\widetilde M_{ij}\to M_j$. Composition with an isomorphism preserves its separated etale property and the square remains cartesian. Both overlap squares now use the same $f_{ij}$, exactly as required by the gluing lemma.

source.place: Tag 0DUS (lemma-etale-separated-over-well-nigh-affine); first overlap paragraph in Tag 0DUT.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-etale-local-moduli-gluing] on these charts and their two cartesian overlap squares. In its construction $W=\coprod_i M_i$ and $V=\coprod_{i,j}M_{ij}$ are an etale equivalence relation, and $Q=W/V$ is its fppf sheaf quotient. The lemma supplies the descended map $q:\mathcal X\to Q$, the identities $M_i\times_QM_j\simeq M_{ij}$, and the cartesian comparisons $\mathcal X_i\simeq\mathcal X\times_QM_i$. It also supplies quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, universal homeomorphism, and the geometric-point bijections for $q$. In particular $q$ is surjective. This is a construction from compatible local presentations, rather than an application of a new finite-inertia coarse-existence assertion.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), overlap equivalence relation and fundamental diagrams Tag 0DUU.

proof.text: For any flat algebraic-space map $Q'\to Q$, put $M'_i=M_i\times_QQ'$ and $\mathcal X'=\mathcal X\times_QQ'$. By step 4 the base change of $f_i$ to $M'_i$ has source $\mathcal X_i\times_QQ'$. Given an algebraic space $T/k$ and $a:\mathcal X'\to T$, uniform categoricality of $f_i$ gives a unique $a_i:M'_i\to T$ whose composite with that base change is the restriction of $a$. On $M'_{ij}=M_{ij}\times_QQ'$ the two restrictions have equal composites with the base change of $f_{ij}$. The map $M'_{ij}\to M_{ij}$ is flat, so uniform categoricality of $f_{ij}$ makes the restrictions equal. The algebraic-space sheaf property glues the $a_i$ uniquely along the etale cover $(M'_i\to Q')$ to $b:Q'\to T$. The equality $bq_{Q'}=a$ is checked after the covering $(\mathcal X_i\times_QQ'\to\mathcal X')$; the same local uniqueness proves uniqueness of $b$. Thus $q$ is uniform categorical, and taking $Q'=Q$ proves the required coarse universal property for every algebraic-space target, without a separation assumption on $T$.

source.place: Final paragraph of Tag 0DUT, categorical descent after an arbitrary flat algebraic-space base change; overlap uniqueness written explicitly.

proof.text: We next prove adequacy on each $M_i$. Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-invariant-rank-strata] to $(U_i,R_i)$: it gives finitely many invariant open-and-closed affine pieces $(U_{i,n},R_{i,n})$ of positive constant degree $n$. Write $E_i=\prod_n E_{i,n}$ and $L_i=\prod_n L_{i,n}$. Invariance of the pieces makes both arrow homomorphisms coordinatewise. Thus an element $(e_n)_n$ is in $C_i$ exactly when $s_n^\sharp(e_n)=t_n^\sharp(e_n)$ for every $n$, giving $C_i=\prod_n\operatorname{Eq}(E_{i,n}\rightrightarrows L_{i,n})$. Consequently $M_i$ is the disjoint union of the corresponding affine $M_{i,n}$, and $f_i$ is the disjoint union of their invariant-spectrum maps. For each piece the local groupoid theorem again gives a quasi-compact quasi-separated map with global function ring exactly $\Gamma(M_{i,n},\mathcal O)$. If $U_i$ is empty there are no pieces and the assertion is vacuous. The etale-locality criterion allows this open-and-closed refinement of the adequacy check.

source.place: Tag 03BI (groupoids-lemma-finite-locally-free-disjoint-free); Alper Proposition 8.2.1, justification of the constant-rank reduction.

proof.text: Fix a nonempty piece, write $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$, $R=\operatorname{Spec}L$, $\mathcal Z=[U/R]$, and let the common positive degree be $n$. For any surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal Z$, [lem-sfb-affine-groupoid-quasicoherent-algebra-descent] identifies it with a surjective equivariant map $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ of $E$-algebras and identifies global sections with invariant elements. Given $b\in B^R$, choose a lift $a\in A$. Form the affine groupoid over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ by pulling the descent datum of $A$ through the original groupoid. Its arrow algebra is $L_A=A\otimes_{E,t^\sharp}L$, with the other structure map obtained using $\beta_A$. The two projections are base changes of the original projections, hence finite locally free of degree $n$. The identity, inverse and composition are induced by the identity and cocycle equations for $\beta_A$.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), affine algebra form; Alper Proposition 8.2.1, first two paragraphs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-invariant-norm] to this new affine groupoid with $\sigma:A\to L_A$ the structural map and $\tau(a)=\beta_A(a\otimes1)$: it gives $z=N_{L_A/A}(\beta_A(a\otimes1))\in A^R$. We claim that $z$ maps to $b^n$ in $B$. On any finite-free chart for $L_A$ over $A$, the norm is the determinant of multiplication by $\beta_A(a\otimes1)$. After reducing $A\to B$, equivariance and $b\in B^R$ turn this multiplier into $b\otimes1$, so its matrix is $bI_n$. The determinant reduces under the ring map by its sum-of-signed-products formula and equals $b^n$. Such charts cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$, so the equality holds in $B$. Thus $z$ corresponds to a global section of $\mathcal A$ lifting $b^n$. This uses positive degree, not division by the stabilizer order, and works for nonreduced rings and group schemes.

source.place: Proposition 8.2.1, norm/characteristic-polynomial computation; groupoids.tex Tag 03BH (lemma-determinant-trick) gives invariant norm, already present in the DAG.

proof.text: Since the surjection and invariant section in steps 7--8 were arbitrary, every nonempty rank piece satisfies the global power-lifting condition. Its map on global functions is an isomorphism by step 6. Apply the affine-target criterion of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] to conclude that every $\mathcal Z\to M_{i,n}$ is adequate. The same lemma first descends adequacy along the open-and-closed covering of $M_i$, and then along the etale covering $(M_i\to Q)$. The latter base changes of $q$ are exactly $f_i$ by the cartesian squares of step 4; $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by that step. Hence $q$ is an adequate moduli space in the stated definition, including power lifting for arbitrary quasi-coherent algebras on every etale base-changed stack.

Finally assume $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ is finite. On every scheme test its base change is finite, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and thus universally closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. These scheme-chart tests say that the stack diagonal is universally closed. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-universal-homeomorphism-separated-target] to the universal homeomorphism $q$ of step 4 to conclude that $\Delta_{Q/k}$ is a closed immersion. Therefore $Q$ is separated over $k$. Steps 4--5 supply the coarse properties and surjectivity; step 9 supplies adequacy. No smoothness of the inertia or invertibility of its order was used.
